references.text: Introduction to the law concerning the firstborn, commanding that all firstborn be consecrated to the Lord.
Restatement of the law to redeem a firstborn donkey with a lamb, and to redeem firstborn sons.
Explains that all firstborn belong to the Lord after He struck down the firstborn in Egypt.
Detailed instructions on the redemption of firstborn humans and unclean animals, including the price of five shekels of silver.
Command to give the Lord the firstborn of sons and of livestock.
Laws concerning firstborn animals and the redemption of unclean animals.
Restatement of the law to consecrate all firstborn male animals to the Lord.
Jesus is presented in the temple as the firstborn, in accordance with the law to consecrate the firstborn to the Lord.
Theological elaboration on the principle that everything firstborn belongs to the Lord, with specification for unclean animals.
Contrast clarifying that only unclean animals and humans are redeemed, while clean animals are holy offerings.
The historical event (the Passover lamb) which is the basis for the command to redeem the firstborn.
Complementary legal requirement confirming that the firstborn belongs to God and must be redeemed.
